To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transient routing loops are a natural consequence of BGP convergence and the duration of the loops are linearly proportional to the minimum route advertisement interval (MRAI).
BGP routing convergence time is the major contributing factor to BGP routing loop duration and BGP routing loop is a direct result of BGP convergence time and MRAI value.

BGP path vector routing information is effective in preventing routing loops but the routing information propagation delay and the MRAI timer value are major factors that contribute loop formation during BGP routing convergence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inter-domain routing loop formation due to BGP's path-vector routing information propagation.

BGP path vector routing convergence and transient routing loops and the results of this paper can be used as a guideline to improve the routing convergence time and to prevent transient BGP routing loops.

the transient routing loops in the Internet are caused by the inherent delay of BGP routing convergence and the MRAI timer.

BGP loop formation is a result of the routing convergence process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BGP loop formation can be minimized by reducing the MRAI values, and by using BGP enhancements to speed up routing convergence.
the duration of inter-domain routing loops is primarily determined by BGP's routing information propagation speed and the routing information inconsistency between the BGP nodes.
BGP's routing loop behavior is closely related to its routing convergence behavior and the loop duration is directly proportional to BGP MRAI value.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transient routing loops can be a major cause of routing instability at the inter-domain scale.
BGP routing loops are not caused by any specific BGP feature or protocol behavior.
the transient loops are not due to BGP's design, but are caused by BGP's slow convergence.
